data.title: After the group meeting
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for staying after the group meeting. I'm Noor Haddad, I run the humidity sensor array at the Fenwick Institute. Speaker 2: Of course. You wanted the cleaned logs from the rooftop sensors? Speaker 1: Yes, please, before Thursday's group meeting, so I can show the drift plots. Speaker 2: I'll send you the cleaned logs before Thursday. Speaker 1: Great. And I've asked the workshop to book the climate chamber for us; they said they'd confirm by Monday. Speaker 2: Then I'll chase them if we haven't heard by Monday. Speaker 1: Perfect.

data.title: Call from the garage
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Hi, it's Rhys Talbot at Ferncliff Motors. We ran the diagnosis on your car. Speaker 2: How bad is it? Speaker 1: The gearbox is terminal, I'm afraid; it needs replacing, not repairing. Speaker 2: Ouch. When can you do it? Speaker 1: Bring it in Tuesday morning at eight and we'll have it back to you by Thursday. Speaker 2: I'll drop it off Tuesday at eight. Speaker 1: And keep the tow receipt; your insurer may cover the tow. Speaker 2: Good point. I'll call the insurer about the tow claim this week.

data.title: Volunteer orientation
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Welcome aboard. I'm Beatrix Olowe, I coordinate the volunteers at St Aldric's Hospital. Speaker 2: Thanks, I'm looking forward to it. Speaker 1: You'll be on the oncology ward's reading cart on Saturdays, so the patient-confidentiality module has to be done before your first shift on the 24th. Speaker 2: I'll finish the confidentiality module before the 24th. Speaker 1: And bring your vaccination record to the orientation on Monday; occupational health checks everyone's. Speaker 2: I'll bring it on Monday. Speaker 1: Lovely. The cart has large-print books, if anyone asks.

data.title: Talk at the Python meetup
data.transcript: Speaker 1: I'm Ilse Marchetti, I run the Harbourside Python meetup. Your lightning talk on leaked credentials was the best thing at the last one. Speaker 2: Thank you. The breach data was all from public dumps, nothing private. Speaker 1: Would you give the full version in November? I need the abstract by Friday for the schedule. Speaker 2: Yes, I'll send you the abstract by Friday. Speaker 1: Great. We can sometimes cover travel for speakers, but check the reimbursement page first. Speaker 2: I'll look up the reimbursement policy.

data.title: Hallway, aerospace department
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Do you have a minute? It's about chapter two. Speaker 2: Of course, Professor Varenne. Speaker 1: The outline still mixes the thermal model with the test results. Send me a revised outline before our meeting on the 24th. Speaker 2: I'll send the revised outline before the 24th. Speaker 1: Also, the graduate office closes thesis-title registrations on the 31st. Speaker 2: I haven't registered mine yet. I'll do that this week. Speaker 1: Good.

data.title: Storyboard review with Bluefen
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Mateus Corrin from Bluefen Studio. The client liked the storyboard, but frames six to nine need the new logo. Speaker 2: I can turn those around. I'll send you the revised frames by Wednesday. Speaker 1: Great. Legal is still reviewing the contract on our side; I'll get you the signed copy this week. Speaker 2: Thanks. I'll chase you on Friday if it hasn't come through. Speaker 1: Fair. And we should get lunch when this wraps. Speaker 2: Definitely, we should.

data.title: Call with The Meridian Dispatch
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Freya Aldous here, I edit The Meridian Dispatch. Your note on meteor showers would suit the December issue. Speaker 2: I'd be glad to write it. Speaker 1: Eight hundred words, and I need it by the 25th to lay out the issue. Speaker 2: You'll have it by the 25th. Speaker 1: If you have a photo of the Perseids, we'd run it. Speaker 2: The best one is the astronomy club photographer's; I'll ask her if we can use it.

data.title: Talvera Aerospace screening
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Anouk Severin from Talvera Aerospace. The ground-segment team would like a panel interview on the 30th. Speaker 2: That works. Speaker 1: Before then we run a standard background check, criminal records and references, for every candidate. I'll send the consent form; please return it signed by Thursday. Speaker 2: I'll sign it and send it back by Thursday. Speaker 1: The panel likes candidates who come with questions about their tooling. Speaker 2: Then I'll prepare a couple of questions on their mission-control software before the 30th.

data.title: Astronomical society committee
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Callum Breck, treasurer. I still need the receipts for the eyepiece order to close the quarter. Speaker 2: Sorry. I'll send you the receipts tonight. Speaker 1: Thanks. And for the December star party, the school only takes hall bookings until the 15th of November. Speaker 2: I'll book the hall, then. Speaker 1: Good.

data.title: Call with Tamsin
data.transcript: Speaker 1: It's Tamsin. Moving day is Saturday; the old tenant only left yesterday. Speaker 2: Do you still need the van? Speaker 1: Yes, can you rent one for Saturday morning? Speaker 2: I'll book the van for Saturday. Speaker 1: And boxes; we're short. Speaker 2: I'll pick up packing boxes on Friday and bring them over. Speaker 1: You're a lifesaver.

data.title: Coffee with Esme
data.transcript: Speaker 1: It's been ages! Esme Whitlock; we overlapped at the old job. Speaker 2: Esme! How's Quillon Analytics? Speaker 1: Good, but I'm looking to move. Is your team hiring? Speaker 2: We are, actually. I'll introduce you to our hiring manager this week. Speaker 1: That would be wonderful. Oh, and you have to read The Salt Archive; it's the best novel I've read this year. Speaker 2: I'll look it up. We should do this more often. Speaker 1: We really should.

data.title: Poster with Kwabena
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Kwabena here. The conference wants poster PDFs uploaded to their portal by the 27th. Speaker 2: I'll upload ours by the 27th, once the final figure is in. Speaker 1: I'll send you the final figure tomorrow. Speaker 2: Great. I also want to read their poster guidelines; last time our fonts were too small. Speaker 1: Good idea.

data.title: Grant report check-in
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Rosalind here. Can you send me the figures for the grant report by Friday? The funder wants the report on the 23rd. Speaker 2: Yes, I'll send them on Friday. Speaker 1: Thanks. I should tell you why I've been patchy: we're on our third round of IVF, and I'm at the clinic most mornings this month. Please keep it to yourself. Speaker 2: Of course. I'm sorry it's been so hard. Take whatever time you need. Speaker 1: Just the figures, really, and I'll do the rest.

data.title: Lunch
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Before the others get here: this stays between us. The company is cutting the telemetry team next month, and it won't be announced until the 3rd. Your role is safe, but Bertrand's and Lucia's aren't. Speaker 2: That's awful. Do they know? Speaker 1: Not yet, and they can't hear it from us. I need you to quietly write handover notes for the telemetry dashboard by the end of the month. Speaker 2: I'll write the handover notes by the end of the month.

data.title: Call with Marguerite
data.transcript: Speaker 1: I need a favour, and it's a hard one. The divorce is final, but Luc is contesting custody of the twins, and the hearing is on the 29th. Speaker 2: I'm so sorry. What can I do? Speaker 1: My lawyer says character references help. Would you write one about me as a parent? Speaker 2: Of course. I'll write it this weekend and send it to you. Speaker 1: Thank you. Please don't mention any of this to the others yet.

data.title: Morning, at the gate
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Sorry to stop you so early. Our son was arrested on Saturday; it's a misunderstanding, but he's been charged. Speaker 2: Ezra, that's terrible. Is he all right? Speaker 1: He's home, but we need a good criminal defence lawyer, and you know people. Speaker 2: I'll send you the name of the lawyer who helped my colleague, today. Speaker 1: Thank you. We're not telling anyone on the street.

data.title: Mentoring session
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Can I be honest about why the milestone slipped? I've been having panic attacks, and my doctor has just started me on medication. Speaker 2: Thank you for telling me. Your health comes first. Speaker 1: Could we move the thesis milestone by a week? Speaker 2: Yes. I'll move your milestone to the following week and tell the committee only that the schedule changed. Speaker 1: Thank you, that really helps.

data.title: Call with Corvane
data.transcript: Speaker 1: This is between us and the board. We have eight weeks of runway, and if the bridge round doesn't close we can't make December payroll. Speaker 2: That's serious. Who knows? Speaker 1: Only the board, and now you. Do you know anyone who structures bridge loans? Speaker 2: I'll send you the contact of the adviser who helped my last company, by Wednesday. Speaker 1: Thank you.

data.title: Workshop planning
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for making time. I want to get the small-satellite thermal workshop settled before the venue starts chasing us. Shall we go through the list? Speaker 2: Please. I have the spreadsheet open. Venue first? Speaker 1: Venue first. The Harbour Lecture Theatre holds a hundred and twenty, which is more than we need, and they include the projector and two microphones. They want final catering numbers by the 23rd, and after that the menu is fixed and we pay for whatever we ordered. Speaker 2: I'll confirm the catering numbers with them by the 23rd. Do we have a headcount yet? Speaker 1: Eighty-four registered, and usually about ten percent don't come, so order for eighty. Two vegetarian options, one vegan, and the coeliac speaker needs a separate plate. Speaker 2: Noted. Eighty, two vegetarian, one vegan, one gluten-free. What about the speakers? Speaker 1: Six confirmed. The radiator session has three, the coatings session has two, and the keynote is the person from the materials lab who did the louvre tests. I still need the order of the afternoon sessions and the length of each break, and I want the draft schedule from you by Friday so I can send it to the speakers on Monday. Speaker 2: You'll have the draft schedule by Friday. Forty minutes per talk, twenty for questions? Speaker 1: Thirty and fifteen, I think, or we run late. The keynote can have forty-five. Speaker 1: There's something else, and I'd rather you heard it from me. I'm halfway through chemotherapy, so I won't be able to travel to the venue on the day. I'll join remotely. Please keep it between us; the committee only knows I can't travel. Speaker 2: Thank you for telling me. Of course it stays with me. Then we need the livestream to work properly. Speaker 1: Yes. Remote attendees asked for it last year too. Could you look into a livestream service that doesn't need a technician on site? Something the lecture theatre's own camera can feed. Speaker 2: I'll look up livestream services this week and send you two or three options. Speaker 1: Good. Badges: the print shop needs the final list two days before, so that follows the catering numbers. And the sponsors want their logos on the opening slide, not on every slide. Speaker 2: Opening slide only. I'll tell them when I send the invoices. Speaker 1: Last thing is the budget. We're about three hundred under, so the evening drinks are fine if you want to keep them. Speaker 2: Let's keep them. People talk more at the drinks than in the sessions. Speaker 1: That's true of every workshop I've ever run. Right, I think that's everything for this week. Speaker 2: I'll send the schedule Friday and confirm catering by the 23rd. Speak next week.

data.title: Research group catch-up
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for coming over. I wanted to catch up on the pipeline before the paper revisions start. Speaker 2: Sure. The reprocessing finished last night, so the new config works end to end now. Speaker 1: Great. Could you send me the revised pipeline config? I want to rerun the spectral fits with it. Speaker 2: I'll send it this afternoon. The only change you'll notice is the new outlier threshold. Speaker 1: Which threshold did you settle on? Speaker 2: Three and a half sigma. Three was throwing away real flares, and four kept the cosmic rays. Speaker 1: That sounds right. I'm also writing the section on spectral calibration for the revision, and I'd like you to read it before it goes to the others. Could you review my draft by Monday? Speaker 2: Yes, I'll review it by Monday. Is it the version on the shared drive? Speaker 1: The one dated yesterday. The older one has the wrong wavelength table. Speaker 2: Got it. And the reviewers' second point, about the detector temperature, is that in your section or mine? Speaker 1: Mine, but I need your logs from the cold run to answer it. They don't have to be cleaned. Speaker 2: Fine, they're on the instrument laptop. I'll copy them over with the config. Speaker 1: Thanks. Also, the reading group is ours to choose this month. Speaker 2: I'll pick a paper for the reading group. Something on the new calibration methods, maybe. Speaker 1: Something short, please; people actually read the short ones. Speaker 1: And I need to tell you something strictly confidential. I've filed a harassment complaint against the lab head, and HR has opened an investigation. Nobody else in the group knows, and I'd like to keep it that way until it's resolved. I'm telling you because I may be out of some meetings he chairs. Speaker 2: Thank you for trusting me. It stays with me, and I'll cover anything you need in those meetings. Speaker 1: Thank you. That means a lot. Back to the paper, then: the deadline for the revision is still the 30th? Speaker 2: The 30th, yes. If your section is in by Monday and mine by Wednesday, we have a week for the figures and the response letter. Speaker 1: That's tight but fine. The figure with the flare spectra needs new error bars, by the way. Speaker 2: I'll redo the error bars once the fits are rerun with the new config. Speaker 1: Great. I think that's everything. Thanks again for listening.

data.title: After the club meeting
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for staying after the meeting. I wanted to go through a few things with you before the committee sees the minutes. Speaker 2: Of course. Go ahead. Speaker 1: Right, the treasurer's report, and then something personal, so bear with me. The membership renewals are up on last year, sixty-one paid out of seventy, and the nine who haven't paid have all had two reminders. The launch-day budget is fine: the motors are ordered, the range fees are paid, and the insurance renewal is the only large bill left this quarter. The insurer needs our updated member list before they send the liability certificate, and without the certificate the landowner won't let us on the field, so that is the one thing that has to happen before launch day. The newsletter printing went over by forty, because of the colour pages, but the sponsor covered half of it. The raffle made a hundred and twelve. The cash box is reconciled and the bank statement matches to the penny. The grant from the county arts fund came through at last, three hundred and fifty, and it is ring-fenced for the schools outreach day, so please nobody spend it on motors. The outreach day needs two volunteers with range safety cards, and I have asked twice in the newsletter without a reply. The trailer needs a new tyre before the winter; the quote from the garage was ninety, which I think is fair, and I would like the committee to approve it at the next meeting rather than by email. Our account at the model shop is clear. The equipment loan sheet shows two altimeters still out since September, one with a member who has not renewed, and I would like that one back before anyone else borrows it. The online shop sold eleven badges and four mugs, which barely covers the postage. That is all the small items. That's the money. Now the personal part. I'm going to be declaring bankruptcy next month, after my business failed, and I can't stay on as treasurer while that goes through; it wouldn't be right to keep the club's accounts. Please don't tell the committee why I'm stepping down; I'll say it's for work. I'd like someone to take over the spreadsheet from me this month, and I'll walk them through every tab. It's not complicated, but the reconciliation sheet has a few quirks that I should explain in person rather than in writing, and I would rather hand it over properly than leave a mess. Speaker 2: Gareth, I'm sorry. Of course I'll keep it to myself. I'll take over the treasurer's spreadsheet; walk me through it whenever suits you. Speaker 1: Thank you. Next week, then. And the safety briefing for launch day, could you draft it by the 30th? The range officer wants to see it a week before. Speaker 2: I'll draft the launch-day safety briefing by the 30th. Speaker 1: And would you ask the insurer about the liability certificate? I'd rather not be the one emailing them right now. Speaker 2: I'll ask the insurer for the updated liability certificate this week. Speaker 1: Thank you. That's a weight off.

data.title: Corridor, after stand-up
data.transcript: Speaker 1: I need to tell someone. My visa expired in August and the renewal was refused, so I'm here without status while my lawyer appeals. Please don't say anything to HR. Speaker 2: I won't. That must be frightening. Speaker 1: It is. For the appeal I need a reference letter about my work. Speaker 2: I'll send you a reference letter by Friday. Speaker 1: Thank you.

data.title: Hallway
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Can you keep something quiet? I'm pregnant, and I haven't told our manager yet; I'm waiting until after the twelve-week scan. Speaker 2: Congratulations! My lips are sealed. Speaker 1: The thing is, I'll be on leave in March, so could you lead the March workshop instead of me? Speaker 2: Yes, I'll take the March workshop. Speaker 1: Thank you. I'll send you my slides next month.

data.title: Call with Bram
data.transcript: Speaker 1: About the reunion dinner: I'm ninety days sober now, and I'd rather not be somewhere with an open bar. Not many people know I was in treatment. Speaker 2: I'm proud of you, Bram. Leave it with me. Speaker 1: Thanks. Could you find somewhere that doesn't centre on drinks? Speaker 2: I'll book an alcohol-free venue for the reunion by next week. Speaker 1: That means a lot.
